messages:
Anya (PM): Heads-up — a couple of enterprise customers and a public competitor announcement pushed feature-parity pressure onto our roadmap. They specifically called out per-route cost controls, model-level A/Bing, and a simplified function-calling UX. We need to decide what we pull into Q2.
Mike (Eng): Can you share customer asks/examples? engineering-wise per-route cost limits look non-trivial but doable. A/Bing + rollout hooks already on our infra backlog.
Anya (PM): James flagged three customers: FinReg wants per-route spend caps + stronger SLAs; AdStack wants A/B for model variants; DataCo wants function-calling parity (webhook style, easier authoring).
James (Sales): Yup — revenue upside if we ship the spend caps & A/B in a month. FinReg is ready to sign a Dedicated deal if we can guarantee per-route spend controls + audit logs.
Priya (Research): Competitor's announcement is mostly UI sugar + baked-in model variants. Their infra tradeoffs look heavier (no KV cache optimizations). We can win on cost/latency if we don't copy their inefficiencies.
Sofia (Design): For function-calling parity the ask is: single flow for devs to register a tool, test locally, and call via the playground. We can prototype a compact UX that maps to our existing tool schema.
Mike (Eng): Proposed engineering triage: 1) Minimal per-route spend cap (rate + token budget) implemented as policy layer, 2) A/B rollout using existing routing hooks, 3) Lightweight function-calling UX that maps to our tool calling API — no new runtime. Estimate: 6w for (1) + 4w for (2) + 3w for (3) in parallel with 3 engineers and 1 PM.
Anya (PM): Thanks. We need launch criteria for each item. Suggest: per-route caps: enforced for Dedicated & Hosted, audit logs available, tests for SLO adherence. A/B: config API + traffic split + result telemetry in Console. Function-calling: sample library + playground flow + compatibility test harness.
James (Sales): If we can promise those criteria, I can move FinReg & AdStack to close. Also worth noting customers will expect docs & migration guides.
Sofia (Design): UX priority: console visibility first (caps dashboard), then dev flow for function-calls. We can use an iterative release: expose API early, then surface in Console v1.
Priya (Research): Risk: if we rush, we may introduce backend fallbacks that increase tail latency. Recommend a perf gating step: lab run with 5M token/day equivalent.
Mike (Eng): Agreed — add perf gating to the checklist. Also need a rollout plan: canary on Dedicated tenants, then opt-in Hosted customers, auto-fallback to cheaper model variant on overload.
Anya (PM): Drafted a prioritization: A) Per-route spend caps (sales pull + legal), B) A/B rollout + telemetry, C) Function-calling UX (MVP). Defer: embedded pricing changes, advanced on-prem packaging. Thoughts?
James (Sales): Fine with that order. Sales asks we keep ability for fast-tracked Dedicated work for FinReg.
Sofia (Design): Works for me. I'll start wireframes for Console caps dashboard and a tiny function-calling test harness UI.
Mike (Eng): I'll spin up a tech spike for per-route policy & perf gating. Estimated infra changes documented in the spike ticket.
Anya (PM): Action items: @Mike create spike ticket + perf plan by EOW; @Sofia 2 wireframe variants by next Tue; @Priya run competitor perf diff and share notes; @James prepare customer commitment language. We'll reconvene Friday 11am.
ops-bot: Deploy log: canary rollout for routing-hooks service completed on infra-staging at 2026-03-18T09:12:03Z (build 4c9f).
Mike (Eng): noted ops-bot. One more note — if we implement token budget tracking at the gateway we can offer visibility without touching model runtime. That reduces scope.
Anya (PM): Good optimization. Let's aim for gate-level accounting first. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
